blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Written from the City of White Rock's SSMUH page and business licence page, the City of Surrey's SSMUH page and the Province's short-term rental page (as of November 1, 2026). White Rock's own short-term rental rule is not confirmed and is marked as such. Nothing here states a commission, fee or marketing package; those are for Jared to supply.

South Surrey and White Rock share a postal geography, a school system and a view of Semiahmoo Bay, but they are two different governments with two different zoning bylaws. If you are selling, the City that holds your title decides what a buyer can build, so the first question is which side of the line you are on.
This page gives the benchmark prices for the two together, the rules each City set in 2024, what White Rock says about development permits near water and ravines, and what I need to price your home.
South Surrey and White Rock home prices, October 2026

The MLS® Home Price Index benchmark for a typical South Surrey and White Rock home was $996,000 in October 2026, down 5.4% from a year earlier. Detached homes were $1,606,500 (down 6.3% over the year), townhouses $800,900 (down 9.2%) and apartments $558,600 (down 3.5%).

blocks.text: White Rock says it adopted Zoning Bylaw No. 2506 on June 27, 2024, to meet the Province's June 30, 2024 deadline. The City also says off-street parking cannot be required on lots in its six-unit areas.
Development permit areas in White Rock

White Rock's page says areas within its Watercourse, Flood Plain, Ravine and Significant Trees Development Permit Areas need a development permit. For a seller on the hillside or near the creeks, that is a detail a builder will ask about, and one you should know before you describe the lot as redevelopable. The City also says restrictive covenants on title still apply and that SSMUH rules do not legalize a suite built without a building permit.

Short-term rentals

Surrey's own rule is on my Surrey page: a $358 annual business licence and a principal-residence requirement, with stays under 90 consecutive days. White Rock's business licence page says a licence is needed for any activity for gain or profit, including residential rentals, cites Business Licence Bylaw 1997, No. 1510, and sets a fine of $200 a day for operating without a valid licence. It does not mention short-term rentals by name.

The Province's rule sits on top of anything White Rock and South Surrey requires. The Province says the principal residence requirement applies in municipalities with a population of 10,000 or more. A short-term rental can only be the host's usual home, "where they make their home day-to-day," plus one secondary suite or accessory dwelling unit on the same property. A bed and breakfast is allowed only if the owner lives on the property.

Any rental for fewer than 90 consecutive days must also be registered with the Province, one registration number per unit. The Province lists the fee as $100 a year for a host's principal residence and $450 a year for a secondary unit such as a suite or cottage, and compliance with local bylaws is a condition of registration.

faq.q: Which City's rules apply to a South Surrey house?
faq.a: The City of Surrey's. South Surrey is part of Surrey, so Zoning Bylaw No. 12000 applies, with amendments adopted July 8, 2024. White Rock has its own Zoning Bylaw No. 2506, adopted June 27, 2024.

faq.q: How many units can be built on a White Rock lot?
faq.a: The City of White Rock says a minimum of three units on a lot of 280 m² or less, four on a larger lot and six on a lot of 281 m² or more within 400 m of a prescribed bus stop. Covenants on title and development permit areas still apply.

faq.q: Does White Rock have Transit Oriented Areas?
faq.a: The City says that at the time of its page, White Rock has not been designated to have any.

faq.q: Can I sell a White Rock house with an unpermitted suite?
faq.a: You can, but the City says the 2024 rules do not legalize a suite built without a building permit. It must be brought into BC Building Code compliance or decommissioned.

The City's business licence page says a licence is needed for residential rentals and cites Business Licence Bylaw 1997, No. 1510. The Province requires a short-term rental to be the host's principal residence, plus at most one suite or accessory unit, and registered.
